content: Naftifine hydrochloride is a topical medication prescribed to treat fungal skin infections, including athlete's foot (tinea pedis), jock itch (tinea cruris), and ringworm (tinea corporis). In some cases, it may be prescribed for other conditions; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Naftifine is available in two forms: a cream and a gel. The cream is typically applied once daily, while the gel is applied twice daily, in the morning and evening. Treatment duration usually ranges from 2 to 4 weeks, but certain infections may require up to 6 weeks of therapy. Follow the instructions on your prescription label precisely. If you have any questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Use the medication exactly as prescribed; do not apply more or less than directed or use it more frequently than instructed. Before application, clean the affected area thoroughly and allow it to dry. Apply a thin layer of the medication and gently rub it in until most of it is absorbed. Use only enough to cover the infected area. Wash your hands after applying the medication unless the treatment is for your hands. Continue using naftifine for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve. Do not discontinue use without consulting your doctor. Before using naftifine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to naftifine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins and supplements, that you are currently taking. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while using naftifine, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Naftifine may cause side effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following symptoms: itching, burning, irritation, stinging, redness, dryness, or rash. If you experience a severe adverse reaction, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store naftifine in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly; consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. Naftifine is intended for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest the medication. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin products to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If your symptoms persist after completing the prescribed course of treatment, contact your doctor. Keep all follow-up appointments with your healthcare provider. If you have any questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Naftifine is marketed under the brand name Naftin®.
